core_obligations: Let Y -> X be a morphism from a scheme whose image lies in T (proof lines 3247-3248).
Show that Y x_X X' is an algebraic space whose image in |X'| lies in T' (proof lines 3248-3249).
Identify Y x_{X_{/T}} X'_{/T'} with Y x_X X', which is the cartesian property (proof lines 3249-3251).
Conclude the representability of X'_{/T'} -> X_{/T} (statement lines 3242-3243).
proof_roadmap: Pull back and identify the representing object (proof lines 3248-3251).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism f : X' -> X of algebraic spaces over S, a closed subset T of |X| and T' its inverse image in |X'|, the lemma asserts that the square relating the completions X'_{/T'} and X_{/T} to X' and X is cartesian, and that consequently X'_{/T'} -> X_{/T} is representable by algebraic spaces (statement lines 3230-3244). The proof tests the statement on a scheme Y over X whose image lies in T, shows that Y x_X X' is an algebraic space whose image lies in T', and concludes that the functor Y x_{X_{/T}} X'_{/T'} is represented by Y x_X X', which is the cartesian property (proof lines 3246-3251). The level is H2: the test-object reduction and the identification of the representing object are both displayed.
